Georgian court begins hearing lawsuit seeking ban on major opposition parties A court ​in Georgia opened hearings on Wednesday in a lawsuit filed by the government seeking outright bans on the five main opposition parties, in a move that civil society ‌groups say presages the beginning ​of one-party rule in the South Caucasus country. The Constitutional Court in the Black Sea city of Batumi will meet for three days to review the suit, first filed by the ruling Georgian Dream party a year ago. The court, whose ruling is final and cannot be appealed in Georgia, must give its decision by June 2027. The Ebola species behind the outbreak kills about half of those infected and has no approved treatment or vaccine. Since the first cases were confirmed in Democratic Republic of Congo in May, the disease has killed 4,646 people. Health officials fear misinformation and funding shortfalls could fuel further spread within the region and across borders. items.excerpt: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian yesterday said he told Pakistani Army Chf. Field Mar. Asim Munir that there would be no talks with the United States until Iran’s demands were met. According to an Iranian readout of the meeting, Munir also met Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, who said the United States could not regain Tehran’s trust until it fulfilled seven conditions Iran set out last month for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Menna Alaa El-Din and Yasmine Ghania report for Reuters. IRAN WAR – YEMEN Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis today denied launching any drones towards the Saudi holy city of Medina. The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen earlier said it had intercepted drones over Medina and the wider Eastern region. Nayera Abdallah reports for Reuters. ... Israeli strikes and gunfire in two separate incidents in Gaza yesterday killed at least four people, according to local health officials. The IDF later said that Akram Yassin, who was killed alongside his wife, was a senior official in Hamas’ general security apparatus in Gaza which was tasked with protecting senior Hamas officials, but did not comment on the two gunfire incidents, one of which killed a 17-year-old boy. Nidal al-Mughrabi reports for Reuters. RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR ... Ukrainian police today said four people were killed in overnight Russian attacks that targeted energy facilities across four regions. Two of the dead were in the capital Kyiv, while the other two were killed outside the northeastern city of Kharkiv. Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said Russia had attacked power facilities in the Kyiv, Volyn, Odesa, and Mykolaiv regions, as well as civilian enterprises in at least two other regions. Dan Peleschuk reports for Reuters. ... Russia’s Defense Ministry yesterday said the Russian military struck three cargo vessels in Ukraine’s port of Reni, and two other cargo vessels en route to Odesa. Russian forces also hit two logistics hubs in Ukraine’s northwestern Volyn region and in the city of Khmelnitskiy. JekaterĪna Golubkova reports for Reuters. U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff today met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg, Russia and presented him with an updated proposal to end the war in Ukraine, a U.S. official told Axios. Witkoff yesterday met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and other European representatives in Norway, and following the meeting Zelenskyy said the next step should be a trilateral meeting between himself, Putin, and Trump, a format that Russia has so far rejected. Reuters reports; Barak Ravid reports. Russia today released U.S. citizen Stephen James Hubbard from Russian custody in an act of goodwill before Putin’s meeting with Witkoff. Trump yesterday said he had asked Putin to release Hubbard. Hubbard was seized from his home in Ukraine months after Russia invaded Ukraine and was accused of being a mercenary. The United States has maintained that the charges against Hubbard were fabricated. Lucy Papachristou reports for Reuters; Luke Broadwater reports for the New York Times. ... French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu yesterday said the country will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for upcoming protests over underfunding of education in the country and wider issues planned on Saturday. Lecornu acknowledged the government’s failures in its response to last weekend’s violence and said the deployment “will be massive.” French President Emmanuel Macron today pledged to prevent a repeat of the weekend’s riots. Elizabeth Pineau and Dominique Vidalon report for Reuters; Elizabeth Pineau and Dominique Patton report for Reuters. Australian lawmaker Helen Haines, who was hit by a car on Monday in what authorities say was a deliberate attack, has lost both her legs, her husband confirmed today. Phil Haines added that “her heart and mind are in good shape” and that the “good news in all this is that she’s alive.” The alleged attacker Brendan Nugent appeared in court today on charges of dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. Lana Lam and Katy Watson report for BBC News. Burkina Faso’s Justice Ministry today said their parliament yesterday adopted a revised penal code that restores the death penalty. The revised code reintroduces the death penalty for crimes including terrorism, espionage, treason, and importing expired or banned products that result in death. Reuters reports. ... Meta yesterday said it has complied with an order from Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court for the company to give equal treatment on its platforms to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and opposition candidate Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro before Sunday’s presidential runoff. Meta added that the restrictions ordered by the court “do not affect organic posts.” Mauricio Savarese reports for AP News. U.K. Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh today said “following careful consideration,” the government has made the decision to approve production at Jackdaw gas field off of the east coast of Scotland. Fahnbulleh added that Jackdaw will start supplying gas to homes from as early as the end of the month. Jackdaw was initially approved for production in 2022 but has faced years of litigation and pushback from environmental groups, who insist that more drilling would hamper efforts to cut carbon emissions, and production would not protect energy security. Environment Program report published today said countries are not doing enough to cut emissions that cause climate change, and that the United States sticks out as the only major country where planet-warming pollution increased dramatically last year. The United States was tied with Russia as the G20 countries with the most per capita emissions of carbon dioxide and other planet-warming gases. The report also warned that global warming is now projected to exceed previous estimates, with even the most optimistic scenario seeing average temperatures rise to 1.7-1.8 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by mid-century. Rebecca Hersher reports for NPR; Simon Jessop reports for Reuters. ... items.title: Oct. 21: Midwest inflation outpaces the nation, which was up 3.7% | Banking & Finance | fwbusiness.com
items.excerpt: Oct. 21: Midwest inflation outpaces the nation, which was up 3.7% | Banking & Finance | fwbusiness.com # Oct. 21: Midwest inflation outpaces the nation, which was up 3.7% * By Mike Marturello mmarturello@kpcmedia.com #### MIke Marturello * Author email (mmarturello@kpcmedia.com) * Oct 21, 2026 * 3 mins ago * 0 FORT WAYNE — Inflation in the Midwest has outpaced the nation, said data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Inflation, as measured by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics’ consumer price index, was up 4.2% in September for the Midwest while the national rate was 3.7%. Gasoline had a highest annual increase of 35.5% in the Midwest compared to 34.2% nationally year over year. On a monthly basis, costs jumped 0.6% from August to September, the biggest gain in five months, up from a 0.4% increase the previous month. The figures underscore the lingering impact of the Iran war on gas prices and the stubborn persistence of inflation, which has ticked higher since the war began in late February. “Inflation in the 3% range has proven to be a rather stubborn feature of the American economy in the past five years. And if employers aren’t providing adequate cost-of-living increases, workers are finding their paychecks just don’t stretch as far as they did a few years ago, leaving them with tough decisions on how to cover household expenses,” said Rachel Blakeman, director of the Community Research Institute at Purdue University Fort Wayne. “Things are going to be especially hard as we head into the holiday spending season as families and households balance costs vs. income and use of credit cards. With CPI well north of 3%, we can expect to see the Federal Reserve respond with higher interest rates as we close out 2026 and head into 2027.” The rise isn’t all linked to oil and gas, as surging investment in data centers and AI has also pushed up prices for computer chips and the consumer electronics that use them. Elevated inflation has posed political problems for Republicans in Congress and is a challenge for the Federal Reserve, which is required by Congress to seek stable prices, The Associated Press reported. “With early voting now open in Indiana and many other states, we can expect to see voters taking their frustration about higher prices with them to the polls, just as they did in 2024,” said Blakeman. Excluding the volatile food and energy categories, core prices rose 2.6% in September from a year ago, up from 2.4% the previous month and higher than economists had expected. And they climbed 0.3% from August to September, an elevated pace that, if it continued for a year, would run well above the Fed’s 2% target. Higher inflation will likely put more pressure on the Fed to lift its key interest rate at its next meeting Oct. 27-28. Economists noted that the report showed price increases were spread more broadly across the economy than in recent months. “The report was worse than expected,” Bill Adams, chief U.S. economist at Fifth Third Bank, said in a note to clients. “Price increases were widespread ... affecting a range of durable goods, nondurables, and services.” Backing out the volatile energy and food sectors, Midwestern prices were up 3% in the Midwest and 2.6% nationally. Other notable year-over-year increases: • Household energy up 7.7% in the Midwest and 6.2% nationally with electricity up 8.8% regionally compared to 4.4% nationally. • Rent up 4.3% in the Midwest while nationally it was a 2.8%. • Food away from home (restaurants) was up 4.3% regionally and 3.5% in the United States. • Grocery increases were less in the Midwest with food at home up 1.5% compared to 1.8% nationally. Mike Marturello is the executive editor of KPC Media Group. **www.FWBusiness.com** 600 W. Main St. Fort Wayne, IN

items.title: Grocery Prices Sit 22% Above 2021 Levels as Near-Record Diesel Raises Costs From Farm to Store
items.excerpt: Grocery Prices Sit 22% Above 2021 Levels as Near-Record Diesel Raises Costs From Farm to Store ... September price data show food at home costs 22.5% more than five years ago, while diesel above $6 a gallon adds pressure that has not fully reached store shelves. Americans are paying about 22% more for groceries than they did five years ago, and the latest federal price data arrived as diesel — the fuel that powers tractors, freight trucks and refrigerated trailers — holds near its record high. The Bureau of Labor Statistics' food-at-home index stood at 321.758 in September 2026, compared with 262.695 in September 2021, a 22.5% increase, according to BLS figures compiled by the St. Louis Fed. The monthly picture looks calmer. Grocery prices slipped 0.1% in September and were 1.8% higher than a year earlier, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported in its latest Consumer Price Index release. But a slower annual rate does not erase five years of accumulated increases, and several of the foods most closely tied to a balanced diet are still rising faster than the grocery average. Fuel is what makes the next few months hard to call. The national average price of diesel was $6.33 a gallon on Oct. 16, up 68% from $3.76 before the U.S.-Iran war began, according to AAA figures cited by the Associated Press. Diesel hit a record $6.53 in September. No federal agency has yet measured how much of that cost will reach retail food prices, and economists quoted by the AP said much of it has not shown up so far. ... The September report shows a split grocery aisle. Fresh fruits were up 4.9% from a year earlier, fruits and vegetables overall rose 3.7%, coffee climbed 7.1%, and beef rose 3.5%, according to the BLS detailed tables. Eggs fell 20.6%, and dairy dipped 0.7%, which helped hold the overall grocery figure down.

items.title: US inflation rose slightly last month after 2 years of steady cooling but remained low
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — Inflation in the United States ticked up in October, driven by costlier rents, used cars and air fares, a sign that price increases might be leveling off after having slowed in September to their lowest pace since 2021. Consumer prices rose 2.6% from a year earlier, the Labor Department said Wednesday, up from 2.4% in September. It was the first rise in annual inflation in seven months. From September to October, prices edged up 0.2%, the same as the previous month. Excluding volatile food and energy costs, “core” prices rose 3.3% from a year earlier, the same as in September. From September to October, core prices rose 0.3% for a third straight month. Over the long run, core inflation at that pace would exceed the Fed’s 2% target.

An executive order by President Donald Trump had called on the Bureau of Prisons to revise its medical care policies so that federal funds aren’t spent “for the purpose of conforming an inmate’s appearance to that of the opposite sex.” The new policy, blocked earlier by a lower court, would halt surgeries, taper off hormones and end social accommodations like makeup and wigs. As we delve deeper into the day's news, we find ourselves reminiscing about classic films, thanks to Julia Stiles' emotional reunion with her '10 Things I Hate About You' castmates on 'Dancing With the Stars', which included a heartfelt tribute to the late Heath Ledger. Meanwhile, the Access: Horror Virtual Film Festival is pushing boundaries by challenging traditional horror tropes and shedding light on disability in a unique and thought-provoking way, making for a truly diverse and captivating day in the world of film. Addressing a press conference, DCP Raj Tilak Roshan said the five individuals are being brought to Mumbai, taking the total number of arrests in the case to eight so far. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced the decision on Dussehra, ahead of the film’s scheduled theatrical release on November 5, 2026. items.excerpt: Entertainment News (10/21/26) - BusinessWorld Online # Entertainment News (10/21/26) PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. October 20, 2026 | 6:06 pm ## Ziv, VVINK release collaboration PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. Released under Sony Music Entertainment, it is built around Filipino wordplay that links a tricycle’s three wheels to the feeling of being the extra person in someone else’s love story. The song was co-written by Ziv alongside Paolo Benjamin Guico of Filipino folk-pop band Ben&Ben and Angelika Samantha Ortiz, one of the songwriters behind BINI’s hit “Pantropiko.” The mixing was also done by Jacques Jenkins and mastering by Luna Tebbs. The track is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## *Love in Disguise* premieres on Prime Video *LOVE in Disguise*, a Korean series based on the hit web novel *Why Don’t You Know It’s a Girl?*, has premiered on Prime Video. It is directed by Park Dhan-hee and stars Yim Si Wan, Seorina, Kim Junghyun, and Yeonwoo. The genre-blending romance is exclusively seen on Prime Video in the Philippines and in more than 240 countries and territories worldwide. ## Estelle Fly drops club-pop single SINGAPOREAN pop artist Estelle Fly has released “Shut It Down,” a playful club-pop single about switching off the overthinking and making the dance floor your own. Inspired by the Rihanna and Kesha songs, the new release is an invitation to let loose, dance with friends and have fun even when life feels complicated. It is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## Cayabyab, APO, Mitch Valdes reunion THIS holiday season, National Artist for Music Ryan Cayabyab, OPM legends APO, and performer Mitch Valdes will come together for *naRyan nAPO Kami*, the fourth chapter of the MaestroClass Concert Series. The shows will be held on Dec. 4, 5, and 6 at the Proscenium Theater at Rockwell Center, Makati. All shows take place at 7:30 p.m. Joined by the Ryan Cayabyab Singers, the special Christmas chapter of the concert series brings together familiar songs, stories, and artists in a celebration that captures the warmth and spirit of a Filipino family gathering. Tickets are available directly at the Proscenium Theater website via *https://prosceniumtheater.com/* and at the Power Plant Mall Cinema. ## *Amir* gets international distribution GMA Pictures, GMA Public Affairs, and Brightburn Entertainment have officially locked in a partnership deal with Columbia Pictures for the distribution of the upcoming fantasy-drama film and 52 nd Metro Manila Film Festival (MMFF) finalist *Amir*. It is directed by Zig Dulay, with a script crafted by National Artist for Film and Broadcast Arts Ricky Lee alongside Anj Atienza. The film’s cast features Dennis Trillo, Argus Aspiras, Glaiza de Castro, Will Ashley, Caprice Cayetano, Epy Quizon, Joel Saracho, Ronnie Lazaro, Laila Ulao, Heath Jornales, Yasser Marta, Mad Ramos, Ethan Hariot, Hebron Ecal, and Mon Confiado. ## Rachel Chinouriri releases new album UK’s indie-pop singer-songwriter Rachel Chinouriri has released her second studio album, I think I spoke too soon, via Atlas Artists/Parlophone Records. items.title: U.S. Premiere of LAIKA's 'Wildwood' to Open 40th AFI FEST | Animation World Network
items.excerpt: LAIKA has set the U.S. premiere of its highly-anticipated new film, Wildwood, at the 40th edition of AFI FEST presented by Canva on Wednesday, October 21, at the TCL Chinese Theatres in Hollywood, two days before the epic stop-motion fantasy hits theaters nationwide through Fathom Entertainment. The film is a long time coming: Travis Knight directs and produces from a screenplay by Chris Butler, based on the novel by Colin Meloy, which LAIKA optioned way back in 2011. Caleb Deschanel handles cinematography; Peyton Elizabeth Lee and Jacob Tremblay lead the voice cast, alongside Carey Mulligan, Academy Award winner Mahershala Ali, Angela Bassett, Awkwafina, Jake Johnson, Charlie Day, Amandla Stenberg, Jemaine Clement, Maya Erskine, Tantoo Cardinal, Tom Waits and Richard E. Grant. ... AFI FEST runs October 21-25 at the TCL Chinese Theatres, with Red Carpet Premieres, Special Screenings, World Cinema, Documentaries and Short Films. The full lineup will be unveiled September 29, individual tickets go on sale October 3, and passes are available now at FEST.AFI.com. The festival is an Academy Awards qualifying festival for the Live Action, Animated and Documentary Short Film categories.
